name: Bobo

inspiration.oldScript: The man in makeup as predator: clown panic that bled into drag panic, a painted face as proof of menace.
inspiration.newLens: A performer who fell on purpose to make a crying kid laugh, and a town that laughed at him instead. The Best ending is laughing with him.

logline: Somebody in Glimmer Falls is having a birthday every night this week, and Bobo is coming to the party. His balloon animals bite, his seltzer bottle stings, and he will not leave until everybody laughs.
backstory: For twenty years Leonard "Lenny" Moffat was Bobo the Birthday Clown, the only clown in Glimmer Falls: size-twenty shoes, a squeaky nose, a bike horn named Honkers and balloon animals in under ten seconds. On July 14, 1979, at Trevor Ashby's seventh birthday at Captain Cheddar's Pizza Cavern in Starlight Mall, the robot mouse band shorted out, the candles caught Bobo's wig, and he fell backward into the ball pit. A Channel 6 crew filming the restaurant's grand opening caught every second. The clip ran on Bay Area Bloopers for three years. Grown-ups chanted "Fall down, Bobo!" at him in the supermarket. The bookings stopped. Lenny closed his little magic shop on Main Street, moved into the apartment above it and never put the nose on again. He is seventy-one now, and every night for seven years he has dreamed of that party. This Halloween the Heartstone has let the dream out. While Lenny sleeps, Bobo walks: eight feet tall, greasepaint grin, balloons with thumbtack teeth, and a terrible need to make the whole town fall down the way he did.

centralIssue.title: Laughed at, never laughed with
centralIssue.summary: Bobo fell down on purpose that day to cheer up a crying kid, and a town turned his kindness into a punchline it never stopped repeating. The nightmare is seven years of humiliation wearing his face. Find out what really happened at the party and give Lenny back the kind of laughter that is shared, not aimed.

poster: A towering clown with a cracked greasepaint grin and a single spinning bow tie looming over a 1980s shopping mall at night, a bouquet of balloon animals with thumbtack teeth in one gloved fist, a party horn in the other, tiny teens fleeing past a pizza restaurant's broken animatronic band
portrait: Close portrait of a sad-eyed old clown in smeared white greasepaint and a scorched rainbow wig, red nose half-cracked, painted smile far wider than his real mouth, a balloon dog with sharp teeth tucked under his chin, lit from below by birthday candles
endingPhoto: A towering clown with a cracked greasepaint grin and a spinning bow tie looming over a birthday party at a pizza parlor at night, balloon animals with thumbtack teeth in his fist, a cake with flickering candles in the foreground, animatronic band animals slumped on stage, teens in party hats sliding under tables
taunts: Honk honk! Who's the birthday kid tonight?
Go on, laugh. Everybody else did.
Pie or seltzer? Wrong answer, it's both!
Fall down, kiddo. Fall down. FALL DOWN.

clues.title: Party Room Three
clues.hint: Captain Cheddar's Pizza Cavern has been gated off in the dead wing of Starlight Mall since 1980. Nobody ever cleared the party rooms.

encounter.title: Happy Seventh, Trevor
encounter.place: Captain Cheddar's Pizza Cavern, Starlight Mall dead wing
encounter.text: Behind the rolling gate, Captain Cheddar's is a cave of dusty skee-ball lanes and tipped-over high chairs. Party Room Three still has a banner: HAPPY 7TH TREVOR. On the stage, the animatronic Cheddar Mouse Band slumps over their instruments, and on the floor of the ball pit lies a scorched rainbow wig. Pinned to the corkboard by the door is a stack of yellowed booking cards, every one stamped CANCELLED.
encounter.art: An abandoned 1970s pizza restaurant party room behind a half-raised mall gate, dusty skee-ball lanes and tipped-over high chairs, a faded crepe-paper birthday streamer still hanging on the wall, an animatronic mouse band slumped over their instruments on a small stage, a scorched rainbow clown wig lying in a dusty ball pit, a stack of yellowed booking slips pinned to a corkboard, a teenager squeezing under the gate with a flashlight, gray dust in the beam, wide shot

choices.label: Squeeze under the gate and read the booking cards

success.text: Forty-one cancellations in August 1979 alone. Notes in the margins: "kids won't stop laughing at the clown," "husband says it'd be embarrassing." Behind them, a letter in shaky pencil to the mall manager: I know I fell. I'll fall again if it makes one sad kid laugh. Please let me keep working. L. Moffat.
success.art: A teenager reading a stack of yellowed cancelled party booking cards by flashlight, a handwritten pencil letter clutched in their other hand

failure.text: The gate rattles down an inch onto your back. Inside, every skee-ball lane lights up at once and the prize counter's plastic spider rings begin to clatter. Something big steps off the stage behind the curtain, and you scramble out on your elbows.
failure.art: A teenager wriggling out from under a rolling mall gate while skee-ball lanes blaze to life behind them and a huge shadow moves behind a stage curtain

choices.label: Reboot the Cheddar Mouse Band and play its memory tape

success.text: The mouse drummer twitches awake and its chest speaker plays the last thing it recorded. Kids laughing. A crash. Grown-ups laughing, a meaner kind. And then, under all of it, a small voice: "Bobo? Are you okay?" And an old man's voice, gentle: "I'm great, Trev. Did I make you smile?"
success.art: A dusty animatronic mouse drummer twitching awake on a pizza restaurant stage, a glowing speaker in its chest, a teenager kneeling with a floppy disk and a tangle of wires

failure.text: The band boots up wrong. The Cheddar Mouse's head turns all the way around and it sings Happy Birthday in a voice made of squeaking balloons. Every candle on every table lights itself. You run.
failure.art: An animatronic mouse singer with its head twisted backward on a dark stage, candles lighting themselves on dusty party tables, a teen fleeing

clues.title: Bay Area Bloopers, Volume 3
clues.hint: Rewind Video still rents the blooper tape that ended Bobo's career. Somebody there knew him.

encounter.title: Clown Catches Fire
encounter.text: Bay Area Bloopers, Volume 3 is the most-rented tape in the store, its box soft from handling. The cover shows a clown mid-tumble with his wig in flames, and the sticker says AS SEEN ON CHANNEL 6! Zelda Fishbein watches you pick it up from behind the counter and does not smile. "That one," she says, "I keep meaning to lose."
encounter.art: A video rental store comedy aisle, a teenager holding a soft, battered videotape box with a painted cartoon of a tumbling clown whose rainbow wig is on fire, rows of comedy tapes behind, and at the rental counter a 63-year-old woman with a silver-streaked black bouffant, cat-eye glasses on a pearl chain and a red vest watching unsmiling, fluorescent store light, medium shot

choices.label: Run the clip frame by frame on the back-room deck

success.text: Frame by frame, it is a different story. The candles catch his wig, sure. But before the fall, Bobo looks at the birthday boy, who is crying while his parents argue behind him. Bobo pats out his wig, winks at the kid, and falls backward into the ball pit on purpose. The laugh track was added later.
success.art: A frozen video still on a monitor of a clown winking at a crying little boy while two adults argue behind them, a teenager leaning close to the screen

failure.text: The tape loops. Fall, laugh, fall, laugh, faster each time, until the laugh track is coming from the speakers in the walls, the ceiling, your own mouth. You eject it and your hands are covered in white greasepaint.
failure.art: A teenager staring at their hands smeared with white clown greasepaint in a dark video store back room, a VHS tape ejecting from a deck

choices.label: Ask Zelda what she knows about the clown

success.text: "Lenny Moffat. He did the kids' matinees when I was still screaming in pictures." Zelda taps the box. "A pratfall is a gift you give somebody who's sad. That tape turned his gift into a punchline and the whole town told it for years. He still lives over his old magic shop on Main. Never comes out."
success.art: A retired scream queen leaning on a video store counter holding an old signed clown headshot, a teenager listening intently, neon open sign glowing behind them

failure.text: Zelda tells you that some things are not her story to tell and rings up a customer. On the TV over the counter, the store's demo tape skips to a clown waving slowly at you through the screen, and nobody else seems to notice.
failure.art: A video store TV mounted above a counter showing a clown waving slowly through the static, customers in line oblivious, a teen frozen in place

clues.title: Trevor's shoebox
clues.hint: The birthday boy from the blooper tape is fourteen now and lives on Crystal Street. He never has parties.

encounter.title: The Kid Who Never Has Parties
encounter.text: Trevor Ashby is fourteen, skinny, and taking apart a lawnmower engine in his garage with total concentration. Everybody on the street knows he is the kid from the clown tape. Everybody on the street has at some point said "Fall down, Bobo" in front of him like it was funny. On the workbench, half hidden under a rag, is a shoebox with a crayon drawing of a balloon dog on the lid.
encounter.art: A skinny fourteen-year-old boy in a grease-stained T-shirt taking apart a lawnmower engine on the floor of a cluttered suburban garage, wrenches spread on a rag, a teenager crouching beside him handing over a wrench, and on the workbench behind them a shoebox half hidden under a rag with a crayon drawing of a blue balloon dog on its lid, a single hanging work light, medium shot

choices.label: Hand him a wrench and help, no questions yet

success.text: After an hour of grease and silence, Trevor opens the shoebox. Inside is a deflated blue balloon dog, a birthday card signed with a honking-horn doodle, and a Channel 6 envelope. "My dad signed the papers so Channel 6 could air it. Mom and Dad were screaming at each other and Bobo kept falling so I'd stop crying. I laughed. Then everybody laughed at him." He wants to say sorry. He never knew how.
success.art: Two teenagers in a garage sitting on overturned buckets, an open shoebox between them holding a deflated blue balloon dog and an old birthday card, late afternoon light

failure.text: Trevor sees you looking at the shoebox and shoves it under the bench. "I know what you want. You want to hear about the clown. Everyone does." He pulls the garage door down between you, and you hear a bike horn honk once, softly, from inside.
failure.art: A garage door rolling shut on a teenager's angry face, a single squeaky bike horn visible on the workbench behind him

choices.label: Offer him a trade for a look inside the shoebox

success.text: Kev knows Trevor has been hunting a rare carburetor gasket for a month. One gasket later, the shoebox is open: the balloon dog, the honking card, and Trevor's seven-year-old handwriting on a note he never mailed. Dear Bobo, I'm sorry they laughed at you. I laughed WITH you. Love, Trevor.
success.alone: A little asking around tells you Trevor has been hunting a rare carburetor gasket for a month. One gasket later, the shoebox is open: the balloon dog, the honking card, and Trevor's seven-year-old handwriting on a note he never mailed. Dear Bobo, I'm sorry they laughed at you. I laughed WITH you. Love, Trevor.
success.art: A paperboy handing over a small engine part in a garage while a teenage boy opens a shoebox to reveal a child's handwritten apology note and a deflated balloon dog

failure.text: Trevor laughs, not nicely. "You think I'd sell it?" He tucks the box under his arm and leaves on his bike. Halfway down the street, a red balloon drifts down out of a clear sky and follows him, bobbing, all the way to the corner.
failure.art: A boy biking down a suburban street with a shoebox under his arm, a single red balloon drifting after him through a cloudless sky

signature.title: The Balloon Zoo
signature.text: There is a balloon dog on your doormat. Then a balloon giraffe on the mailbox, a balloon poodle on the porch rail, and a whole squeaking zoo going up your stairs to your bedroom door. They turn to look at you when you come home, rubber necks creaking, and you see that every one of them has a mouthful of thumbtacks.
signature.art: A suburban porch and front staircase at midnight crowded with brightly colored twisted balloon animals, a blue balloon dog on the doormat, a balloon giraffe on the mailbox, a balloon poodle on the porch rail, a squeaking line of balloon animals climbing the stairs inside, every one turning its rubber head toward a teenager in the doorway and showing rows of thumbtack teeth, yellow porch light, wide shot

choices.label: Grab a safety pin and pop your way upstairs

success.text: Pop, pop, POP. Giraffes, poodles, a very offended swan. You fight your way to your door in a blizzard of rubber scraps and slam it behind you. On the other side, a horn honks twice, almost impressed.
success.art: A teenager charging up a staircase through bursting balloon animals with a safety pin, colorful rubber scraps flying like confetti

failure.text: Every balloon you pop lets out a laugh, a recorded grown-up laugh, the kind from the tape. By the top of the stairs the whole house is laughing at you. You lie awake with your pillow over your ears.
failure.art: A teenager in bed with a pillow pressed over their ears, popped balloon scraps on the floor, ghostly laughing mouths floating in the dark room

choices.label: Crouch down and pet the balloon dog on the doormat

success.text: It flinches, then leans into your hand with a squeak. Its thumbtack teeth fold away. It is blue, like the one in Trevor's shoebox, and it trots off down the street, looking back to see if you will follow. The rest of the zoo deflates with a sad, long sigh.
success.art: A teenager gently petting a blue balloon dog on a doormat, its sharp teeth folding away, a basset hound sniffing it curiously, the other balloon animals sagging

failure.text: It bites. Not hard, but enough. When you look at your hand, there is no wound, only a smear of white greasepaint and a perfect red circle like a clown nose on your knuckle. It does not wash off until Tuesday.
failure.art: A teenager staring at a red clown-nose circle and white greasepaint smear on their knuckle, a balloon dog with tack teeth squeaking on the doormat

choices.label: Skip the stairs and climb the trellis to your window

success.text: You shimmy up the rose trellis, roll through your window, and lock it. Downstairs, the zoo waits all night for you to come up the stairs like a sucker. In the morning they have blown away down the street like leaves.
success.art: A teenager climbing a rose trellis to a second-floor window at night while balloon animals wait in a line on the staircase inside

failure.text: The trellis is made of balloons tonight. It squeaks, stretches, and lowers you very gently back down onto the lawn, right into the middle of the zoo. They form a ring around you and wait for you to do a trick.
failure.art: A teenager being lowered onto a lawn by a stretching trellis made of twisted balloons, a ring of balloon animals with sharp teeth gathering around

signature.title: The Laugh Track
signature.text: The TV turns itself on to a test pattern. Then the laugh track starts. You drop a cup and the room roars with recorded laughter. You say "what the heck" and the audience howls. Down the block, every TV on Crystal Street is laughing too, and in the dark hallway of your house, something in size-twenty shoes takes one squeaky step closer.
signature.art: A dark 1980s living room at one in the morning lit only by a boxy television showing a color-bar test pattern with pale laughing studio audience faces flickering over it, a dropped cup on the carpet, a teenager standing frozen by the couch, and in the dark hallway doorway a pair of enormous red size-twenty clown shoes stepping forward, cold blue TV glow, medium wide shot

choices.label: Take a bow and laugh along louder than the track

success.text: You bow. You do a pratfall onto the couch. You laugh so loud and real that the canned track stumbles. Laughing at yourself, with yourself, is a sound it does not know how to copy. The TV flickers off, and in the hallway the shoes shuffle back, uncertain.
success.art: A teenager doing a theatrical pratfall onto a couch, laughing wildly, a TV screen flickering out, giant clown shoes shuffling backward in a dark hallway

failure.text: Your laugh comes out wrong, a nervous squeak, and the track loves it. It replays your squeak a hundred times, faster and higher, until a gloved hand reaches around the doorframe and squeezes a bike horn right next to your ear.
failure.art: A white-gloved hand reaching around a doorframe to squeeze a bike horn beside a startled teenager's ear, a TV blaring in the dark

choices.label: Radio your crew to kill every TV on the street

success.text: Bea hits the Lindqvists' breaker, Kev cuts the cable box on the corner, and you yank your own plug. Street by street the laughter dies. In the silence, from the alley, you hear something you did not expect: a big man sniffling, very quietly, like he is trying not to be heard.
success.art: Teens on walkie-talkies throwing breakers and unplugging TVs across a dark cul-de-sac, house windows going dark one by one, a tall clown silhouette slumped in an alley

failure.text: You kill every TV on the street, but the laughter keeps going. It is coming from the neighbors now, standing at their dark windows in pajamas, laughing at you with their eyes closed.
failure.art: Neighbors in pajamas standing at dark windows up and down a suburban street laughing with their eyes closed at a teenager in the road

signature.title: Down in the Drain
signature.place: The storm drain at the corner of Crystal Street, in the rain, 11 p.m.
signature.text: It is pouring, and Kev's whole bundle of Sunday papers has blown out of his bike basket and gone sailing down the gutter like a fleet of soggy boats. The last one swirls into the storm drain on the corner. You crouch to look. Two yellow eyes blink up at you from the dark, and a white glove holds out the newspaper, dry as toast. "Hiya, kiddo! Lose something? Come and get it! Everything down here bounces!"
signature.art: A rain-soaked suburban street corner at eleven at night, newspapers floating down a flooded gutter, a red bicycle with an empty basket at the curb, a teenager crouching at a storm drain in a dripping raincoat, and inside the drain two glowing yellow eyes and a white-gloved hand holding up a perfectly dry rolled newspaper, orange streetlight on wet asphalt, low close medium shot

choices.label: Tell a joke down the drain before he can

success.text: "Why did the clown go to the doctor? He was feeling a little funny." A long silence from the drain. Then a wheeze. Then a big, helpless, honking laugh that echoes up every gutter on the block. The glove sets the paper on the curb, adds a rubber chicken on top, and withdraws.
success.art: A rubber chicken resting on a dry newspaper on a wet curb beside a storm drain, a grinning teenager crouched in the rain, warm laughter glowing up from the drain

failure.text: You fumble the punchline. "Oh, kiddo," says the drain, delighted. "Oh, that was terrible." A recorded laugh track roars up out of every grate on Crystal Street at once, and Kev's newspapers come floating back, every headline now reading the same thing: FALL DOWN.
failure.art: Storm drains along a rainy suburban street glowing with eerie yellow light, a dismayed teenager standing ankle-deep in a flooded gutter surrounded by soggy floating newspapers, porch lights blurred by the rain

choices.label: Reach in fast and snatch the paper back

success.text: You lunge and snatch it. The glove grabs back, there is a ridiculous tug-of-war over the Sunday comics, and you win with a rip, flying backward onto the lawn holding the funny pages. From the drain comes an outraged honk, and then, grudgingly, applause.
success.art: A teenager tumbling backward onto a wet lawn clutching the torn Sunday comics, a white-gloved hand clapping from a storm drain at the curb, heavy rain glittering under a streetlight

failure.text: The glove catches your wrist, gently, and tugs. You slide halfway into the drain on your belly in the rushing gutter water, staring into a dark tunnel lined with floating balloons. Kev hauls you out by the ankles. Your sleeve smells like greasepaint for a week.
failure.art: A teenager lying on their belly in a rushing gutter with one arm inside a storm drain, a paperboy pulling at their ankles, colorful balloons floating in the dark tunnel below

choices.label: Shine a light down the drain to see who's really talking

success.text: Your beam slides past the glove and the yellow eyes, and for a second it shows the truth: an old man in a damp cardigan sitting on a crate in the culvert, a red foam nose in his hand, rehearsing his lines in a whisper. He looks up into the light, ashamed. Then the eyes are back, and the drain is only a drain.
success.art: A flashlight beam shining down a storm drain onto an old man in a damp cardigan sitting on a crate in a culvert, holding a red foam clown nose, looking up in surprise

failure.text: The light shows you a face, an enormous painted grin filling the whole drain from edge to edge, much too close. It honks. You drop the flashlight, and it floats away down the culvert, still on, getting smaller and smaller.
failure.art: An enormous painted clown grin with red lips filling the dark opening of a storm drain, a dropped flashlight still glowing as it floats away down rushing gutter water in the rain

signature.title: Hall of Mirrors
signature.place: The Harvest Carnival funhouse, Glimmer Falls High football field, midnight
signature.text: The Harvest Carnival closed hours ago, but the funhouse lights are still blinking. Inside the hall of mirrors, a hundred of you walk beside you, stretched and squashed and wobbling. Then you notice that every reflection is wearing white greasepaint and a red nose. You stop. They stop. All except one, three mirrors down, which keeps walking, waves, and takes a slow, deliberate pratfall.
signature.art: A neon-lit carnival funhouse mirror maze at midnight, a teenager standing among a hundred warped reflections that stretch and squash, every reflection wearing white clown greasepaint and a red nose, and three mirrors down one reflection taking a slow pratfall while the rest stand still, big scuffed clown-shoe prints in the dust on the floor, colored bulb light, medium wide shot

choices.label: Make the silliest face you can at the one that moved

success.text: You cross your eyes, puff your cheeks and waggle your ears with your thumbs. The rogue reflection freezes. Then it laughs, a real laugh, surprised out of it, and does the face right back. One by one the greasepaint fades off every mirror, and the exit door swings open on the empty fairground.
success.art: A teenager pulling a goofy face with crossed eyes at a funhouse mirror, a clown reflection laughing and copying the face, warped mirrors around them clearing to normal reflections

failure.text: The reflection makes your face better than you do, and all the other reflections turn to watch it. They laugh at you, a hundred of you laughing at one of you, until you find the exit by walking face-first into four mirrors in a row.
failure.art: A hundred warped clown-faced reflections laughing in a neon-lit carnival hall of mirrors, a teenager rubbing their sore nose after walking straight into the glass, colored bulbs blinking overhead

choices.label: Smash your way out of the maze

success.text: Crash, crash, CRASH. You bat your way through six mirrors in a straight line and burst out onto the midway in a shower of silver. Every shard on the grass honks once and goes quiet. Seven years of bad luck, maybe, but tonight you are free.
success.art: A teenager bursting out of a carnival funhouse wall in a shower of silver mirror shards, swinging a baseball bat, a moonlit midway and Ferris wheel behind

failure.text: The first mirror bounces the bat back at you like rubber. So does the second. The whole hall wobbles with laughter and starts to spin, and you stumble out at dawn so dizzy you walk home in a zigzag.
failure.art: A teenager reeling dizzily as a rubbery funhouse mirror bounces their baseball bat back at them, the whole mirrored hallway spinning around them in swirls of pink and teal neon light

choices.label: Follow the size-twenty scuff marks on the floor

success.text: Big floppy prints in the dust, always turning left. You follow them past the mirrors to a little door marked PERFORMERS and a tiny dressing room. On the vanity sits a jar of greasepaint, a wig on a foam head, and a snapshot of Bobo crouched beside a sobbing little boy at a party, holding out a blue balloon.
success.art: A cramped backstage dressing room behind a funhouse, a vanity with a jar of white greasepaint, a red wig on a foam head, and an old snapshot of a clown kneeling beside a crying little boy

failure.text: The prints lead you in a perfect circle back to where you started. Then a second set appears beside your own feet, matching you step for step, and stays with you all the way home.
failure.art: Giant clown shoe prints in dust circling a dim funhouse floor, a second set of enormous floppy prints appearing step by step beside a nervous teenager's sneakers, warped mirrors glinting on every side

signature.title: Have You Checked the Birthday Kid?
signature.place: The Okafor house on Crystal Street, babysitting, 11 p.m.
signature.text: Little Ada Okafor is finally asleep and you are halfway through a bag of cheese puffs when the kitchen phone rings. A squeaky honk, then a cheerful voice: "Is the birthday kid asleep yet? I have a delivery!" You hang up. It rings again. "Have you checked the birthday kid?" Upstairs, very faintly, a bike horn goes honk honk. The phone cord, you notice, is stretched taut across the kitchen and up the stairs.
signature.art: A cozy 1980s suburban kitchen at eleven at night, a teenage babysitter holding a yellow wall phone receiver, the coiled phone cord stretched tight across the kitchen and up a dark staircase into the upstairs hallway, an open bag of cheese puffs on the counter, a toddler's drawing on the refrigerator, warm stove light and a dark stairwell, medium shot

choices.label: Go up and tell Ada a bedtime story about a kind clown

success.text: You sit on Ada's bed and tell her about a clown who fell down on purpose to make a sad kid laugh. Halfway through, the closet door creaks open an inch and stays there, listening. By the end Ada is asleep, and on her nightstand sits a balloon flower that was not there before, with a tag: FOR THE STORYTELLER.
success.art: A teenager sitting on a child's bed telling a story by lamplight, a sleeping little girl, a closet door open a crack with a glimpse of a gloved hand, a balloon flower on the nightstand

failure.text: You start the story, and the closet starts doing the voices. All of them. Badly. Ada laughs herself awake and demands an encore, and you spend until midnight trading lines with a closet while a horn honks on every joke you get wrong.
failure.art: A giggling little girl bouncing on her bed as a closet door glows with a painted clown grin inside, a frazzled teenager babysitter holding a storybook

choices.label: Pick up and ask him if his refrigerator is running

success.text: "Is your refrigerator running?" A pause on the line. "Uh... yes?" "Then you'd better go catch it!" Silence. Then, from the line and from upstairs at once, the wheezy, honking laugh of a man who has not been pranked in seven years. "Good one, kiddo," he says, and hangs up for the night.
success.art: A teenager grinning into a yellow wall phone in a dim 1980s kitchen at night, the coiled cord stretched up the stairs, a giant clown shadow doubled over laughing on the staircase wall

failure.text: "Oh, I know that one," says the voice. "Mine's better." The refrigerator door bangs open and a jack-in-the-box springs out of the vegetable drawer right at your face. You scream so loud Ada wakes up and has to calm you down.
failure.art: A jack-in-the-box clown springing out of the vegetable drawer of an open refrigerator at a screaming teenager, a calm little girl in pajamas standing in the kitchen doorway holding a teddy bear

choices.label: Scoop up Ada and run for the neighbors' porch

success.text: You take the stairs three at a time, wrap Ada in her blanket and bolt out the back door to the Delgados' porch light. Mrs. Delgado lets you in without a question. When you check through the window, every light in the Okafor house is on, and a single balloon is bobbing at the front door, waiting politely.
success.art: A teenager carrying a blanket-wrapped little girl across a moonlit backyard toward a neighbor's glowing porch light, a lone balloon bobbing at the door of the house behind

failure.text: You fling open the front door and run straight into a birthday party: streamers, a cake, a dozen neighbors in paper hats singing to Ada in her pajamas. Ada loves it. You stand there frozen as a huge gloved hand puts a party hat on your head, and keeps it there.
failure.art: A teenager frozen in a doorway holding a little girl as a surprise birthday party fills a suburban living room, neighbors in paper hats, a huge gloved hand placing a party hat on the teenager's head

signature.title: A Party in Your Honor
signature.place: Captain Cheddar's Pizza Cavern, three a.m.
signature.text: You wake up at a birthday party. It is yours. Captain Cheddar's is lit up like 1979, and everyone you know is wearing a paper hat and smiling stiffly at a cake with seven blue candles. The robot band plays Happy Birthday in the wrong key. Then the kitchen doors bang open and Bobo ducks through them, eight feet tall, holding a cream pie in one hand and a seltzer bottle in the other. "Everybody laugh!" he roars.
signature.art: A garish 1979 pizza restaurant birthday party at three in the morning, a teenager in pajamas at the head of a long table, friends in paper party hats smiling stiffly around a cake with seven blue candles, an animatronic mouse band playing on a small stage, and an eight-foot sad-eyed clown in smeared white greasepaint, a scorched rainbow wig and a cracked red nose bursting through the kitchen doors holding a cream pie and a seltzer bottle, bright colored party lights, wide shot

choices.label: Step in front of your friends and take the pie yourself

success.text: Splat. Cream in your hair, your eyes, your ears. You lick your lips and give a thumbs-up. Your friends stare, then start to laugh, and it is a warm, real, are-you-okay laugh. Bobo lowers the seltzer. Under the greasepaint, for one second, an old man looks like he might cry.
success.art: A teenager with a face full of cream pie giving a thumbs-up, friends in party hats bursting into warm laughter, a towering clown lowering a seltzer bottle in surprise

failure.text: You step up, but your friends get it anyway, all of them, pie after pie after pie, until the whole party is dripping and nobody is laughing. You wake with the taste of cream and a headache that lasts all day.
failure.art: A whole birthday party of teens dripping with cream pie, every face stony, a clown juggling more pies behind them

choices.label: Blow out the candles and wish for him, not you

success.text: You wish that Bobo could have one good birthday party again. The blue flames go out. The robot band switches to a sweet, slow song. Bobo stands very still in the middle of the room, then pulls a single blue balloon from his pocket, twists a dog, and leaves it at your plate.
success.art: A teenager blowing out seven blue candles on a cake, a towering clown standing still in a quiet pizza restaurant, twisting a single blue balloon dog

failure.text: The candles relight themselves. And again. And again. "Trick candles!" Bobo hoots, and the room laughs at you blowing and blowing until you are dizzy and gasping on the sticky floor.
failure.art: A dizzy teenager slumped beside a birthday cake whose blue trick candles keep relighting, a clown pointing and laughing, paper hats everywhere

choices.label: Dive into the ball pit and tunnel for the exit

success.text: You dive under the plastic balls and crawl. The pit is deeper than it should be, and down near the bottom you find a scorched old wig and a pair of glasses. You come up behind the prize counter, by the exit, holding Lenny Moffat's spectacles and a first-aid kit you grabbed off the wall on the way.
success.art: A teenager surfacing from a deep ball pit beside a prize counter, holding a pair of old wire glasses and a scorched rainbow wig, a party raging in the background

failure.text: The ball pit has no bottom. You sink and sink through red, yellow and blue, and somewhere far above you hear a whole birthday party shouting "Fall down! Fall down!" in perfect time.
failure.art: A teenager sinking through an endless ball pit of red, yellow and blue plastic balls, a distant ring of party-hat faces looking down from above

signature.title: Everything Down Here Floats
signature.text: You are brushing your teeth when you hear it: a giggle, deep down the bathroom drain, and a voice like a kazoo in a tunnel. "Psst. Hey, kiddo. Wanna see a trick?" The sink gurgles, burps and erupts in a fountain of rainbow confetti, streamers and tiny paper party hats that pours over the counter and fills the tub knee-deep. Your folks walk past the open door, look right at the mess and say goodnight like there is nothing there. From the drain, the voice chuckles: "Grown-ups never get the good tricks."
signature.art: A small suburban bathroom at midnight, the sink erupting in a fountain of rainbow confetti, paper streamers and tiny paper party hats pouring over the counter, the bathtub filled knee-deep with confetti, a teenager in pajamas frozen with a toothbrush in their mouth, two parents in bathrobes walking past the open doorway smiling, warm vanity light, medium shot

choices.label: Lean over the drain and ask if he's okay down there

success.text: "Hey," you say into the drain. "Are you okay down there?" The confetti stops in midair and drifts down like snow. A long silence, then a small, tired voice: "Nobody asks the clown that, kiddo." By morning the bathroom is spotless, except for one blue paper party hat sitting on your pillow.
success.art: Rainbow confetti hanging still in midair and drifting down like snow in a quiet bathroom, a teenager leaning gently over the sink drain, a single blue paper party hat resting on the counter

failure.text: The drain answers with a big honking laugh, and a second gusher hits you full in the face. You spend an hour picking glitter out of your eyebrows. In the morning there is still glitter in your ears that only you can see.
failure.art: A gusher of rainbow confetti and glitter blasting a teenager full in the face over a bathroom sink, streamers tangled in their hair, a toothbrush flying from their hand

choices.label: Grab a party horn out of the confetti and blow a trick right back

success.text: You fish a party blower out of the confetti and give a long, rude toot down the drain. A shocked pause. Then the drain toots back, twice, and the two of you go back and forth like a duet until you are both wheezing. The confetti curls itself into one neat bow on the faucet.
success.art: A teenager in pajamas blowing a curly party horn into a bathroom sink drain, an answering puff of confetti shooting back up, streamers curling into a neat bow on the faucet

failure.text: Your toot comes out as a sad little raspberry, and the drain howls with laughter. The confetti rises around you like a tide until it reaches your chin. You wake up at dawn in the bathtub, buried in it.
failure.art: A teenager asleep in a bathtub buried up to the chin in rainbow confetti at dawn, a party horn drooping from their lips, streamers draped over the shower rod

choices.label: Jam the stopper in and lean on it with all your weight

success.text: You slam the stopper home and lean. The sink bucks and gurgles and goes quiet with a disappointed squeak. In the silence, very faintly, you hear a slide whistle going down, down, down, like something sliding back into the dark.
success.art: A teenager leaning with both hands on a bathroom sink stopper, confetti settling on the tiles around their feet, the pipes under the sink rattling, a dim nightlight glowing

failure.text: The stopper shoots out like a champagne cork and pings off the ceiling. The confetti geyser lifts you clean off your feet and drops you in the laundry hamper. From the drain comes a delighted honk: "Again! Again!"
failure.art: A rubber sink stopper rocketing toward a bathroom ceiling, a towering geyser of confetti lifting a startled teenager off their feet toward a wicker laundry hamper

signature.title: Fall Down!
signature.place: The Glimmer Falls High pep rally bonfire, 10 p.m.
signature.text: The pep rally bonfire is roaring on the practice field when a sophomore trips over an extension cord and sprawls face-first in the mud. Somebody starts the chant, the one every grown-up in Glimmer Falls learned in 1979: "Fall down! Fall down!" The whole crowd picks it up, parents included, laughing and pointing. With every chant, the balloon animals tied along the bleachers swell bigger and grow thumbtack teeth. At the very top of the stands, in the dark, a pair of size-twenty shoes taps along to the beat.
signature.art: A roaring high school pep rally bonfire on a muddy practice field at ten at night, a sophomore sprawled face-first in the mud by an extension cord, a crowd of teens and parents laughing and pointing, big balloon animals tied along the bleachers swelling with thumbtack teeth, and at the dark top of the stands a pair of huge red clown shoes, a teenager pushing through the crowd, orange firelight, wide shot

choices.label: Flop down beside the kid and turn the fall into an act

success.text: You flop into the mud next to the sophomore, wave your legs in the air and announce, "And for our next trick!" The kid catches on, laughing, and the two of you do a sloppy double cartwheel to wild applause. The chant breaks into real cheering. Up in the stands the big shoes stop tapping, and somebody blows one soft honk of approval.
success.art: Two muddy teenagers cartwheeling side by side in front of a roaring bonfire, a crowd in the bleachers cheering and clapping, balloon animals shrinking on their strings, big clown shoes resting in the shadows

failure.text: You flop into the mud and the crowd only chants louder, now at both of you. The balloon animals strain at their strings, grinning. You help the kid up, and you both slink off behind the band bus, muddy to the eyebrows.
failure.art: Two mud-covered teenagers slinking away behind a yellow band bus at night, a chanting crowd silhouetted by a bonfire, grinning balloon animals with thumbtack teeth straining at their strings

choices.label: Climb the bleachers and tell the whole crowd to knock it off

success.text: "Hey! KNOCK IT OFF!" Your voice cracks, but it carries. The chant stumbles. Coach Pruitt climbs up beside you and folds her arms, and the parents in the front row suddenly find their shoes very interesting. In the hush, every balloon animal on the bleachers sighs and shrinks, and somebody in the dark at the top of the stands whispers, "Thank you."
success.art: A teenager standing tall on the bleachers pointing at a hushed crowd, a big fierce softball coach with folded arms beside them, deflating balloon animals drooping along the rails, bonfire light on every face

failure.text: Your voice cracks into a squeak, and the crowd turns the chant on you. "Fall down! Fall down!" You don't, quite, but your knees shake all the way home, and a balloon poodle follows you to your door, snapping.
failure.art: A balloon poodle with thumbtack teeth snapping at the heels of a teenager hurrying up a dark suburban sidewalk, distant bonfire glow and a chanting crowd behind them

choices.label: Slip under the bleachers and cut the balloon animals loose

success.text: You crawl under the bleachers through a forest of legs and spilled popcorn and snip string after string. The toothy balloons float up over the bonfire and away into the dark, drifting toward Main Street and a little magic shop with its lights off. The chant fizzles out while everyone tries to figure out where the balloons went.
success.art: Balloon animals drifting up over a bonfire into the night sky toward a small town main street, a teenager with scissors crouched in the shadows beneath wooden bleachers, popcorn scattered on the ground

failure.text: A balloon giraffe notices you snipping. It swivels on its string, thumbtacks bared, and honks an alarm. The whole herd comes down under the bleachers after you, and you spend the night running laps around the practice field.
failure.art: A herd of toothy balloon animals chasing a teenager around a moonlit high school practice field, a balloon giraffe leading the charge, wooden bleachers and a dying bonfire behind

signature.title: Everybody Floats
signature.place: The KGLM water tower, 2 a.m. the night before Halloween
signature.text: Every balloon in Glimmer Falls has slipped its string tonight, and they have all gone looking for kids. From the base of the KGLM water tower you watch your neighbors drift past overhead in their pajamas, lifted by great bunches of balloons, rising toward the catwalk at the top. Up there, against the moon, Bobo stands with a fistful of strings, honking Honkers in time to the circus music pouring out of the radio booth. "Everybody floats, kiddo!" he calls down. "Up here, nobody can laugh at you!"
signature.art: A tall water tower at two in the morning under a huge moon, children and neighbors in pajamas floating up past it on great bunches of colorful balloons, a small radio station booth glowing at the base, and on the catwalk at the top an eight-foot clown in a scorched rainbow wig holding a fistful of balloon strings and a brass bicycle horn, a teenager gripping the tower ladder, silver moonlight, low wide shot

choices.label: Get Mix to open the phone lines for the town's good Bobo memories

success.text: Mix puts you on the air: "Glimmer Falls, if Bobo ever made your birthday, call in." The switchboard lights up like a pinball machine: a mechanic who still has the balloon dinosaur's photo, a nurse whose sick little brother got a free show. Each story floats up to the catwalk on the tower speakers, and the balloons sink gently, setting kids down on the lawns one bunch at a time. At the top of the tower, Bobo sits down with his face in his gloves, listening.
success.alone: You talk your way onto the air: "Glimmer Falls, if Bobo ever made your birthday, call in." The switchboard lights up like a pinball machine: a mechanic who still has the balloon dinosaur's photo, a nurse whose sick little brother got a free show. Each story floats up to the catwalk on the tower speakers, and the balloons sink gently, setting kids down on the lawns one bunch at a time. At the top of the tower, Bobo sits down with his face in his gloves, listening.
success.art: A radio booth switchboard blazing with lit call buttons, a teen DJ and a teenager at the microphone, children drifting gently down onto lawns on sinking balloons, a clown seated on a water tower catwalk with his face in his gloves

failure.text: The phones stay dark. One caller gets through, and all he wants is to chant "Fall down, Bobo" before Mix cuts him off. Up on the catwalk the honking gets louder, and another bunch of balloons lifts off from Crystal Street.
failure.alone: The phones stay dark. One caller gets through, and all he wants is to chant "Fall down, Bobo" before you fumble the dump button. Up on the catwalk the honking gets louder, and another bunch of balloons lifts off from Crystal Street.
failure.art: A dark radio switchboard with one blinking call button, a teen DJ wincing at the microphone, another bunch of balloons lifting a child off a suburban street toward a moonlit water tower

choices.label: Climb the tower ladder and catch the floating kids by their ankles

success.text: Rung after rung, wind in your face, you snag a pajama ankle here and a sneaker there, untying balloons and passing kids down to your crew below. By the time you reach the catwalk, there is nobody left to catch. Bobo looks at you, out of breath and furious and holding his last balloon, and lets it go himself.
success.art: A teenager climbing a water tower ladder at night, catching a floating child in pajamas by the ankle, friends below reaching up, a towering clown on the catwalk releasing one last balloon into the moonlight

failure.text: Halfway up, a gust swings you out over Crystal Street, hanging on by one hand. A bunch of balloons bumps into you, friendly, and ties itself to your belt loop. You float up to the catwalk and stand with the others until dawn.
failure.art: A teenager dangling by one hand from a water tower ladder high above moonlit suburban rooftops, a bunch of bright balloons tying itself to their belt loop and tugging them upward

choices.label: Hook the loose strings to Joey's tow truck winch and reel everyone in

success.text: Joey backs the tow truck up to the tower, and you run across the lawns gathering trailing strings like kite tails and hooking them to the winch. The cable hums. One by one, slow and steady, the floating kids are reeled down to the grass, giggling and dizzy. Up top, Bobo watches his whole sky clear out, and honks once, sadly.
success.alone: The junkyard tow truck is parked by the tower with its winch unlocked, and you run across the lawns gathering trailing strings like kite tails and hooking them on. The cable hums. One by one, slow and steady, the floating kids are reeled down to the grass, giggling and dizzy. Up top, Bobo watches his whole sky clear out, and honks once, sadly.
success.art: A rusty tow truck at the base of a water tower at night, its winch reeling in dozens of balloon strings, children in pajamas drifting down to the grass, a teen mechanic working the levers

failure.text: The winch reels in, the balloons pull up, and the tow truck's front wheels lift off the asphalt. Joey says a word his grandmother would not approve of. The truck bobs in the air until sunrise, with both of you sitting on its roof.
failure.alone: The winch reels in, the balloons pull up, and the tow truck's front wheels lift off the asphalt. You say a word your grandmother would not approve of. The truck bobs in the air until sunrise, with you sitting on its roof.
failure.art: A rusty tow truck floating off the ground beneath an enormous cluster of balloons at dawn, two teenagers sitting glumly on its roof, a water tower rising behind them

finale.title: The Last Laugh
finale.place: Starlight Mall food court, Halloween night
finale.text: On Halloween night the Starlight Mall food court has become a three-ring circus. Everyone who ever chanted at him is frozen mid-laugh in a spotlight, mouths wide, unable to stop: grown-ups from the supermarket, the Channel 6 anchorman, Trevor's dad. Balloon animals the size of station wagons prowl between the tables. And in the center ring, on stilts, Bobo swings a giant mallet. "Go on," he says, and his voice cracks. "Laugh. Everybody else did."
finale.art: A neon mall food court on Halloween night turned into a three-ring circus, grown-ups frozen mid-laugh in white spotlights with mouths wide, balloon animals the size of station wagons prowling between the tables, and in the center ring an eight-foot sad-eyed clown on stilts in smeared white greasepaint, a scorched rainbow wig and a cracked red nose swinging a giant wooden mallet, four teenagers in homemade costumes below him, a skinny boy holding a deflated blue balloon dog, spotlight and neon, wide shot

choices.label: Knock his stilts out from under him

success.text: You swing low and the stilts crack. Bobo topples like a circus tent and bursts into a cloud of confetti and rubber scraps. The spotlights go out. The frozen grown-ups slump over their trays, blinking, with no idea why their faces hurt.
success.art: A teen swinging a bat at a giant clown's stilts, the clown toppling and bursting into confetti and balloon scraps over a mall food court

failure.text: He steps over your swing like a man stepping over a puddle. The mallet comes down beside you with a cartoon BONK, and the whole circus laughs. You hear yourself laughing too.
failure.art: A giant mallet slamming the floor beside a dazed teen, a stilted clown towering overhead, frozen grown-ups laughing in the spotlights

choices.label: Out-clown the clown with a banana peel and a seltzer ambush

success.text: You lay the peel. Glory distracts him with a high kick. Bobo steps, slips, and goes down in the greatest pratfall the food court has ever seen, and the giant balloons pop in sympathy. The circus folds up like a cheap pop-up tent and is gone.
success.alone: You lay the peel and distract him with the highest kick you can manage. Bobo steps, slips, and goes down in the greatest pratfall the food court has ever seen, and the giant balloons pop in sympathy. The circus folds up like a cheap pop-up tent and is gone.
success.art: A giant clown slipping on a banana peel in a mall food court while a drag queen high-kicks beside him, car-sized balloon animals popping in the background

failure.text: He sees the peel, picks it up, and eats it in one bite. "I invented that one, kiddo." The seltzer bottle turns toward you.
failure.art: A towering clown eating a banana peel with a wink, a seltzer bottle swinging toward a teen in a Halloween costume

choices.label: Bring Trevor forward with the balloon dog and laugh with Bobo, not at him

success.text: Trevor walks into the center ring holding the deflated blue dog. "You fell down so I'd stop crying. It worked. I'm sorry they laughed at you." You play the slowed-down tape on the mall TVs, the wink and all. Then your whole crew does the worst pratfall in history, on purpose, all at once, and laughs, together. Bobo laughs too, a real laugh, and the stilts sink, the greasepaint melts, and the eight-foot nightmare shrinks into an old man in striped pajamas, sleepwalking, waking up in the food court with tears on his face.
success.art: A teenage boy offering a deflated blue balloon dog to a shrinking clown in a mall food court, teens in costumes sprawled in a deliberate pile laughing, an old man in pajamas waking up as the greasepaint melts away

failure.text: Bobo cannot hear Trevor over seven years of laughter. The balloon dog slips from the boy's hand and floats up into the dark. You have the truth, but he needs to see it, not just hear it.
failure.art: A deflated blue balloon dog floating up out of a boy's hand into the dark rafters of a mall, a towering clown turning away

choices.label: Answer his gag with a gag of your own, the way you traded tricks that first week

success.text: That first week, on your doorstep and down the drains, you learned that Bobo cannot leave a setup hanging. So you cup your hands and yell up at him, "Knock knock!" The mallet stops mid-swing. "Who's there?" "Interrupting cow." "Interrupting c..." "MOO!" It is terrible, and the frozen grown-ups laugh at the joke instead of at him, and Bobo loses his rhythm on the stilts, sits down hard on the edge of the center ring, giggling helplessly, while the whole circus sags around him like a tired balloon.
success.art: A giant clown on stilts sitting down hard on the edge of a circus ring in a mall food court, wheezing with laughter, a costumed teenager grinning up at him, huge balloon animals sagging and deflating

failure.text: "Knock knock." "Who's there?" Your mind goes completely blank. The whole circus waits, and then it laughs at you, and Bobo laughs loudest. You still have the timing; you just need the punchline.
failure.art: A costumed teenager frozen in a spotlight in the middle of a circus ring in a mall food court, mouth open, a giant clown on stilts laughing above them, frozen grown-ups laughing at the tables

choices.label: Shut the jeering down cold, like you did midweek when the town's laughter turned mean

success.text: Midweek you learned what feeds him: laughter aimed like a thrown rock, from TV sets, funhouse mirrors and a chanting crowd. So you plant your feet in the center ring and roar at the frozen grown-ups, "STOP LAUGHING AT HIM!" One by one their mouths close, and the spotlights dim with nothing left to shine on. Bobo stands on his stilts in the sudden quiet, mallet raised over nobody, and slowly lowers it, and the circus collapses around him like a tent with its pole pulled out.
success.art: A costumed teenager standing firm in a circus ring shouting at a crowd of grown-ups who fall silent, dimming spotlights, a giant clown on stilts slowly lowering a huge mallet, a striped tent collapsing overhead

failure.text: You shout, but the laughter is seven years deep and it rolls right over you. The mallet comes down with a cartoon BOING an inch from your sneakers. The grown-ups are still laughing, but a couple of them look embarrassed about it, which is a start.
failure.art: A giant wooden mallet slamming down beside a costumed teenager's sneakers in a circus ring, a clown on stilts looming, laughing grown-ups in spotlights, two of them covering their mouths sheepishly

choices.label: Tell the kind-clown story you told the night before Halloween, then fall down laughing together

success.text: You step into the center ring and tell it the way the night before Halloween taught you: the balloon dinosaur that lasted a week, the free show for a sick kid, the clown who fell down on purpose so a crying boy would laugh. Trevor steps up beside you, and the frozen grown-ups start remembering out loud, their own birthdays, their own Bobo. When the last story is told, your whole crew takes the worst pratfall in history, together, on purpose, and the food court laughs the right way, warm and with him. Bobo laughs too, a real laugh, and shrinks down off his stilts into an old man in striped pajamas, waking up surrounded by people who are glad to see him.
success.art: An old man in striped pajamas laughing with tears on his face in a mall food court, a crew of costumed teenagers sprawled in a joyful pile beside him, smiling grown-ups gathering close, deflated balloons on the floor

failure.text: You start the story, but the frozen laughter is too loud, and Bobo cannot hear the kind parts over it. He turns away, mallet drooping. You have the story right; the room just isn't ready to listen.
failure.art: A costumed teenager speaking earnestly in a circus ring while grown-ups laugh frozen in spotlights, a giant clown on stilts turning away with his mallet drooping, balloon animals prowling between tables

best.title: Laughing With You
best.text: The Glitter Box throws Trevor Ashby the seven-years-late seventh birthday party he never got, and Lenny Moffat comes in a fresh red nose. He makes a balloon dog for every kid in Glimmer Falls, falls down exactly once, and the room laughs the right way, warm and together, with him. Channel 6 runs a correction. By Christmas Bobo is doing Saturday shows at the children's ward in Sacramento, and Trevor helps him carry Honkers.
best.art: A crowded small theater birthday party under streamers, an old clown with a fresh red nose and a neat rainbow wig handing a blue balloon dog to a grinning skinny teenage boy, kids and drag performers in sequins laughing together around a cake, warm gold party light, medium wide shot

good.title: Party's Over
good.text: Bobo is gone, and the balloons stop showing up on porches. The town forgets the whole week by Thanksgiving. Above the shuttered magic shop on Main, the lights stay off, and Bay Area Bloopers, Volume 3 is still the most-rented tape at Rewind Video. You quietly rent it every week so nobody else can.
good.art: A shuttered small-town magic shop on Main Street at dusk with dark windows above it, a faded painted rabbit and top hat on the glass, a teenager walking past with a rented videotape held behind their back, streetlights just coming on, medium wide shot

bittersweet.title: Honk Once for Help
bittersweet.text: You survive the circus, and so does everyone in the food court. But for months your crew cannot hear a bike horn without flinching, and somebody at school starts chanting "Fall down, Bobo" at Trevor again. Nobody laughs this time, at least. Nobody stops it, either.
bittersweet.art: A high school hallway lined with lockers, a skinny boy standing with his head down while another student jeers at him with hands cupped around his mouth, three teenagers watching uncomfortably from their lockers, a single deflated blue balloon on the floor, flat fluorescent light, medium wide shot

bad.title: Everybody Laugh
bad.text: On November first you wake up in white greasepaint, with a red nose that will not come off and shoes four sizes too big. Every time you speak, the whole town laughs. Your crew is the only one that does not, and they keep trying to wipe your face clean while you smile, and smile, and fall down.
bad.art: A teenager in smeared white greasepaint with a red nose stuck to their face sitting on a suburban curb in oversized clown shoes, two friends kneeling beside them scrubbing at their cheeks with washcloths, neighbors laughing from their porches, late afternoon light, medium shot
